o261: Same meal, two English words. 'Dinner' is the usual word today; 'supper' is an older or more regional word for the evening meal (in some places a lighter, later one). Spanish needs only one: la cena.
o1610: In the example sentence, 'al' is just 'a' + 'el' written as one word (Spanish never writes 'a el'). The 'a' is there because gustar works as 'is pleasing to': 'a el mono le gusta...' = 'to the monkey it is pleasing'. The word itself is el mono.
o2771: A Mexican dish: a corn tortilla dipped in chili sauce, rolled around a filling (often chicken or cheese) and covered with red or green sauce, cheese and cream. You usually see it in the plural: las enchiladas.
